_meta.indication: DARZALEX is a human CD38-directed monoclonal antibody indicated for the treatment of patients with multiple myeloma who have received at least three prior lines of therapy including a PI and an immunomodulatory agent or who are double-refractory to a PI and an immunomodulatory agent

pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, single-arm trial evaluating DARZALEX monotherapy at 16 mg/kg administered with pre- and post-infusion medication until unacceptable toxicity or disease progression
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma who had received at least 3 prior lines of therapy including a PI and an immunomodulatory agent, or who were double-refractory to a PI and an immunomodulatory agent
pivotal_trials.result: ORR 29.2% (95% CI 20.8, 38.9); median duration of response 7.4 months

pivotal_trials.design: Open-label dose-escalation trial of DARZALEX monotherapy at 16 mg/kg until disease progression
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma who had received at least 2 different cytoreductive therapies

nct_ctgov.title: Daratumumab (HuMax®-CD38) Safety Study in Multiple Myeloma

key_safety: Most frequently reported adverse reactions (incidence ≥20%): infusion reactions (48%), fatigue (39%), back pain (23%), pyrexia (21%), cough (21%), nausea, and upper respiratory tract infection
target_moa: First-in-class IgG1 kappa human monoclonal antibody that binds CD38 expressed on multiple myeloma cells, inducing tumor cell lysis via complement-dependent cytotoxicity, antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity, and antibody-dependent cellular phagocytosis

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee meeting was convened; no clinical efficacy or safety issues required one
